answer: To curb Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identities to tidal crustal telemetry. Nodes authenticate by tracking bedrock deformation driven by the ocean tide using an optical sensor fitted with a jade crystal and a cryptographic hardware relic. An attacker must deploy discrete physical sensors per identity, incurring steep manufacturing and geographic installation costs. However, ambient seismic noise can distort the measurements, periodically causing false rejections.
